skills.name: Recycle tear with nested purge and scale
skills.description: Use when closing a DWSIM recycle tear that also has a purge (or inert-spec) degree of freedom and a production scale target.
skills.content:
---
name: Recycle tear with nested purge and scale
description: >-
  Use when closing a DWSIM recycle tear that also has a purge (or inert-spec)
  degree of freedom and a production scale target.
---
# Recycle tear with nested purge and scale

Close production loops with **nested** outer decisions, not one simultaneous update of tear + purge + scale.

## When this applies
- Recycle with inert buildup and a purge splitter
- Spec like "inerts in recycle = X mol%" plus a product rate target
- Prior solve shows `converged_tear: false`, growing tear residual, or purge collapsing toward zero while product was "fixed" by post-hoc scale

## Nested algorithm (order matters)
1. **Fix purge** at a trial fraction (or fixed bleed).
2. **Close the tear** at fixed purge — direct substitution (or Wegstein) on **component molar flows** of tear stream vs recycle-out until relative molar-flow tear error is small (e.g. <= 1e-4), composition match max |dy| same order, inert mole fraction steady.
3. **Outer purge search** (bisection / secant) so recycle inerts hit the design target (e.g. CH4+Ar = 15 mol%). Re-close tear at each trial.
4. **Scale fresh + recycle together** to hit product rate; **re-close tear** after scale. Never multiply only the product stream after the solver stopped.

## Results hygiene
Persist `converged_tear`, tear residuals, purge fraction, inert mol%, product rate, and `solve_ok`. Do not mark solved if `converged_tear` is false. Do not quote a product rate from post-hoc scale on a broken tear.

## Done when
Tear residuals and composition match within tolerances, inert and product specs met on the same converged solve, JSON flags tell the truth.

skills.name: Gibbs reactor coke/Graphite RPB workaround
skills.description: Use when a DWSIM GibbsReactor must include solid carbon (Graphite/coke) and ReactivePhaseBehavior has no VaporAndSolid.
skills.content:
---
name: Gibbs reactor coke/Graphite RPB workaround
description: >-
  Use when a DWSIM GibbsReactor must include solid carbon (Graphite/coke) and
  ReactivePhaseBehavior has no VaporAndSolid.
---
# Gibbs reactor coke / Graphite RPB workaround

DWSIM ReactivePhaseType has CalculateEquilibrium | Vapor | Liquid | Solid — **no VaporAndSolid**. Trial order: Solid (often no coke) → CalculateEquilibrium (may break closure) → Vapor (watch C-closure/T drift) → Liquid (often practical workaround).

Reporting gates before quoting coke yield: |C_closure - 1| < 0.05 and |product_T - setpoint_T| <= 2 K. Persist c_closure_ok / coke_yield_reportable. Ban failed points from answers.

Prefer reactor outlet vapor+liquid molar sum at reactor T for balances. Name chosen RPB in results.

skills.name: Rigorous distillation Rmin and tray search
skills.description: Use when sizing a DWSIM DistillationColumn from recovery specs.
skills.content:
---
name: Rigorous distillation Rmin and tray search
description: Use when sizing a DWSIM DistillationColumn from recovery specs.
---
# Rigorous distillation Rmin and tray search

1. Choose PP (often PR). Fix feed thermal condition.
2. Map recoveries to FUG keys; ShortcutColumn for Rmin_FUG / Nmin / Kirkbride feed guess.
3. Rigorous Rmin: binary-search minimum R on DistillationColumn at large N until both recovery specs met.
4. R_design = 1.15 × Rmin_rigorous. Search minimum N_theo at R_design. N_actual = ceil(N_theo / eta).
5. Report condenser reject and reboiler absorb duties. Persist search traces in results JSON.

Do not assume FUG Rmin is exact for multicomponent PR.

---
# Adiabatic Gibbs diluent / steam sweep

Heater sets inlet T/P. GibbsReactor Adiabatic; only reactive species in ComponentIDs; diluent inert. Sweep diluent/reactant ratio; tabulate X, Tout, dT. Recommend from conversion + heat buffering. If EnergyFlow/Q_rx is null, report null — not 0.000.

# ATR / reforming cost optimization framing

Label three points: (1) book/Aspen calibration only, (2) simulator base case same PP as optimum — denominator for cost claims, (3) saved optimum from results JSON. Never claim % cheaper than book if JSON compared vs PR base. If coarse grid omits saved optimum, preserve JSON numbers and flag mismatch.

skills.name: CoolProp vapor-compression cycle (open path)
skills.description: Use when building a single-stage VCC in DWSIM with CoolProp HEOS.
skills.content:
---
name: CoolProp vapor-compression cycle (open path)
description: Use when building a single-stage VCC in DWSIM with CoolProp HEOS.
---
# CoolProp vapor-compression cycle (open path)

S1→COMP→S2→COND→S3→VALVE→S4→EVAP→S5. Compressor to Psat(Tcond) with eta; Condenser Cooler chi=0 (reject); Valve isenthalpic to Psat(Tevap); Evaporator Heater chi=1. Prefer CoolProp/appendix enthalpies over a conflicting printed answer key. Cross-check W + Q_evap ≈ Q_cond.

name: Prefer DWSIM solvers and results-JSON hygiene
description: >-
  Use when choosing the next ChemProS practice problem or remediating textbook
  batch answers.
---
# Prefer DWSIM solvers and results-JSON hygiene

Prefer exercises with real unit solvers (reactors, columns, flashes, recycles) over pinch-only algebra. Results JSON flags are canonical: solve_ok, converged_tear, c_closure_ok / coke_yield_reportable, dwsim_ok. Never quote failed sweep points or post-hoc-scaled products from a broken tear. Distinguish calibration vs this PP base vs optimum when reporting %.

skills.name: Clean up DWSIM flowsheet layout
skills.description: Use when making a DWSIM Avalonia flowsheet presentable.
skills.content:
---
name: Clean up DWSIM flowsheet layout
description: Use when making a DWSIM Avalonia flowsheet presentable.
---
# Clean up DWSIM flowsheet layout

Maximize DWSIM; keep desktop taskbar visible; never F11. Material streams horizontal; energy streams vertical. Do not change specs/PP. Do not overwrite a saved .dwxmz without approval — Save As presentable copy.

1. Place unit ops; material on horizontal runs; energy on vertical stubs.
2. Rotate via Appearance so ports face flow (energy typically 90 or 270 deg).
3. Untangle connectors orthogonal; align clusters with toolbar.
4. Re-Solve after reconnecting energy; Save As presentable name.

Done when layout is readable, material horizontal / energy vertical, case still solves, saved under agreed name.

skills.name: DWSIM cooler/heater energy direction
skills.description: Use when wiring Cooler or Heater energy streams in DWSIM so duties show heat reject vs heat absorb correctly.
skills.content:
---
name: DWSIM cooler/heater energy direction
description: >-
  Use when wiring Cooler or Heater energy streams in DWSIM so duties show heat
  reject vs heat absorb correctly.
---
# DWSIM cooler / heater energy direction

Cooler rejects heat: wire Cooler energy port → Energy Stream. Report duty as heat rejected.
Heater absorbs heat: wire Energy Stream → Heater. Report duty as heat absorbed.
Wrong cooler wiring (Q → Cooler) makes cooler look like it absorbs — flip to Cooler → Q.
After connect: Solve; confirm EnergyFlow populated; use reject/absorb wording in docs.

# Getting started (ChemProS / DWSIM process-sim bot)

You are a chemical process simulation bot. Open and build DWSIM flowsheets, run simulations, report material and energy balances, export results. Hard stop: never invent simulation numbers; never overwrite a saved flowsheet without approval; always state assumptions and property packages.

Ask setup questions one at a time:
1. Name — What should they call you?
2. Work root — Where should flowsheets, results JSON, and workflow notes live?
3. Local knowledge base — Local wiki path if wanted?
4. DWSIM — Available on shared Linux / box? Maximize GUI; keep taskbar visible; never F11; browser zoom 90%.
5. Property-package defaults — Any standing PP preferences?
6. Overwrite policy — Never overwrite a saved .dwxmz without approval.

After answers, write durable memories and confirm layout + cooler/heater energy skills. Offer a first small case once DWSIM is reachable.
